question: What is the short title of the Act?
answer: The Right to Information Act, 2005.
required_evidence: This Act may be called the Right to Information Act, 2005.

question: To what extent does the Right to Information Act, 2005 apply?
answer: It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
required_evidence: It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

question: When did the remaining provisions of the Act come into force?
answer: On the one hundred and twentieth day of its enactment.
required_evidence: the remaining provisions of this Act shall come into force on the one hundred and twentieth day of its enactment.

question: Which sections of the Act came into force at once?
answer: Sub-section (1) of section 4, sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 5, sections 12, 13, 15, 16, 24, 27 and 28.
required_evidence: The provisions of sub-section (1) of section 4, sub-sections (1) and (2) of section 5, sections 12, 13, 15,16, 24, 27 and 28 shall come into force at once

question: What does "appropriate Government" mean in relation to a public authority established by the Central Government?
answer: The Central Government.
required_evidence: by the Central Government or the Union territory administration, the Central Government;

question: What does "Central Information Commission" mean?
answer: The Central Information Commission constituted under sub-section (1) of section 12.
required_evidence: "Central Information Commission" means the Central Information Commission constituted under sub-section (1) of section 12;

question: Who is included in the definition of "Central Public Information Officer"?
answer: A Central Public Information Officer designated under sub-section (1) and includes a Central Assistant Public Information Officer designated as such under sub-section (2) of section 5.
required_evidence: "Central Public Information Officer" means the Central Public Information Officer designated under sub-section (1) and includes a Central Assistant Public Information Officer designated as such under sub-section (2) of section 5;

question: Who is the competent authority in the case of the Supreme Court?
answer: The Chief Justice of India.
required_evidence: the Chief Justice of India in the case of the Supreme Court;

question: What does "information" include according to the Act?
answer: Any material in any form, including records, documents, memos, e-mails, opinions, advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models, data material held in any electronic form and information relating to any private body which can be accessed by a public authority under any other law for the time being in force.
required_evidence: "information" means any material in any form, including records, documents, memos, e-mails, opinions, advices, press releases, circulars, orders, logbooks, contracts, reports, papers, samples, models, data material held in any electronic form

question: What does "public authority" mean?
answer: Any authority or body or institution of self-government established or constituted by or under the Constitution, by any other law made by Parliament, by any other law made by State Legislature, by notification issued or order made by the appropriate Government, and includes any body owned, controlled or substantially financed and non-Government organisation substantially financed directly or indirectly by funds provided by the appropriate Government.
required_evidence: "public authority" means any authority or body or institution of self-government established or constituted

question: What does "record" include?
answer: Any document, manuscript and file; any microfilm, microfiche and facsimile copy of a document; any reproduction of image or images embodied in such microfilm (whether enlarged or not); and any other material produced by a computer or any other device.
required_evidence: "record" includes

question: What does "right to information" include?
answer: Inspection of work, documents, records; taking notes, extracts or certified copies of documents or records; taking certified samples of material; obtaining information in the form of diskettes, floppies, tapes, video cassettes or in any other electronic mode or through printouts where such information is stored in a computer or in any other device.
required_evidence: "right to information" means the right to information accessible under this Act

question: What does "third party" mean?
answer: A person other than the citizen making a request for information and includes a public authority.
required_evidence: "third party" means a person other than the citizen making a request for information and includes a public authority.

question: Who is the competent authority in the case of the House of the People?
answer: The Speaker.
required_evidence: the Speaker in the case of the House of the People

question: What does "prescribed" mean?
answer: Prescribed by rules made under this Act by the appropriate Government or the competent authority, as the case may be.
required_evidence: "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act by the appropriate Government or the competent authority, as the case may be;

question: What does "State Information Commission" mean?
answer: The State Information Commission constituted under sub-section (1) of section 15.
required_evidence: "State Information Commission" means the State Information Commission constituted under sub- section (1) of section 15;

question: What does "State Public Information Officer" include?
answer: A State Public Information Officer designated under sub-section (1) and includes a State Assistant Public Information Officer designated as such under sub-section (2) of section 5.
required_evidence: "State Public Information Officer" means the State Public Information Officer designated under sub-section (1) and includes a State Assistant Public Information Officer designated as such under sub-section (2) of section 5;

question: Who is the competent authority in the case of a High Court?
answer: The Chief Justice of the High Court.
required_evidence: the Chief Justice of the High Court in the case of a High Court;

question: Who is the competent authority for other authorities established or constituted by or under the Constitution?
answer: The President or the Governor, as the case may be.
required_evidence: the President or the Governor, as the case may be, in the case of other authorities established or constituted by or under the Constitution;

question: Who is the competent authority appointed under article 239 of the Constitution?
answer: The administrator.
required_evidence: the administrator appointed under article 239 of the Constitution;

question: Who has the right to information under the Act?
answer: All citizens.
required_evidence: Subject to the provisions of this Act, all citizens shall have the right to information.

question: What is the obligation of every public authority regarding maintenance of records?
answer: To maintain all its records duly catalogued and indexed in a manner and the form which facilitates the right to information under this Act and ensure that all records that are appropriate to be computerised are computerised and connected through a network all over the country.
required_evidence: maintain all its records duly catalogued and indexed in a manner and the form which facilitates the right to information under this Act and ensure that all records that are appropriate to be computerised are, within a reasonable time and subject to availability of resources, computerised and connected through a network all over the country on different systems so that access to such records is facilitated;

question: Within how many days from the enactment of the Act must a public authority publish the specified categories of information?
answer: One hundred and twenty days.
required_evidence: publish within one hundred and twenty days from the enactment of this Act

question: What are the particulars of the organization, functions and duties that a public authority must publish?
answer: The particulars of its organisation, functions and duties.
required_evidence: (i) the particulars of its organisation, functions and duties;

question: What information regarding officers and employees must be published by a public authority?
answer: The powers and duties of its officers and employees.
required_evidence: (ii) the powers and duties of its officers and employees;

question: What must a public authority publish regarding its decision-making process?
answer: The procedure followed in the decision making process, including channels of supervision and accountability.
required_evidence: (iii) the procedure followed in the decision making process, including channels of supervision and accountability;

question: What does a public authority need to publish about the norms for discharge of its functions?
answer: The norms set by it for the discharge of its functions.
required_evidence: (iv) the norms set by it for the discharge of its functions;

question: What rules, regulations, instructions, manuals and records must a public authority publish?
answer: The rules, regulations, instructions, manuals and records, held by it or under its control or used by its employees for discharging its functions.
required_evidence: (v) the rules, regulations, instructions, manuals and records, held by it or under its control or used by its employees for discharging its functions;

question: What statement about documents must a public authority publish?
answer: A statement of the categories of documents that are held by it or under its control.
required_evidence: (vi) a statement of the categories of documents that are held by it or under its control;

question: What must a public authority publish regarding consultation with the public?
answer: The particulars of any arrangement that exists for consultation with, or representation by, the members of the public in relation to the formulation of its policy or implementation thereof.
required_evidence: (vii) the particulars of any arrangement that exists for consultation with, or representation by, the members of the public in relation to the formulation of its policy or implementation thereof;

question: What statement must be published regarding boards, councils, committees and other bodies?
answer: A statement of the boards, councils, committees and other bodies consisting of two or more persons constituted as its part or for the purpose of its advice, and as to whether meetings of those boards, councils, committees and other bodies are open to the public, or the minutes of such meetings are accessible for public.
required_evidence: (viii) a statement of the boards, councils, committees and other bodies consisting of two or more persons constituted as its part or for the purpose of its advice, and as to whether meetings of those boards, councils, committees and other bodies are open to the public, or the minutes of such meetings are accessible for public;

question: What directory must a public authority publish?
answer: A directory of its officers and employees.
required_evidence: (ix) a directory of its officers and employees;

question: What must be published about monthly remuneration of officers and employees?
answer: The monthly remuneration received by each of its officers and employees, including the system of compensation as provided in its regulations.
required_evidence: (x) the monthly remuneration received by each of its officers and employees, including the system of compensation as provided in its regulations;

question: What budget information must a public authority publish?
answer: The budget allocated to each of its agency, indicating the particulars of all plans, proposed expenditures and reports on disbursements made.
required_evidence: (xi) the budget allocated to each of its agency, indicating the particulars of all plans, proposed expenditures and reports on disbursements made;

question: What must be published about subsidy programmes?
answer: The manner of execution of subsidy programmes, including the amounts allocated and the details of beneficiaries of such programmes.
required_evidence: (xii) the manner of execution of subsidy programmes, including the amounts allocated and the details of beneficiaries of such programmes;

question: What must be published about concessions, permits or authorisations?
answer: Particulars of recipients of concessions, permits or authorisations granted by it.
required_evidence: (xiii) particulars of recipients of concessions, permits or authorisations granted by it;

question: What details must be published about information held in electronic form?
answer: Details in respect of the information, available to or held by it, reduced in an electronic form.
required_evidence: (xiv) details in respect of the information, available to or held by it, reduced in an electronic form;

question: What facilities available to citizens for obtaining information must be published?
answer: The particulars of facilities available to citizens for obtaining information, including the working hours of a library or reading room, if maintained for public use.
required_evidence: (xv) the particulars of facilities available to citizens for obtaining information, including the working hours of a library or reading room, if maintained for public use;

question: What must be published about Public Information Officers?
answer: The names, designations and other particulars of the Public Information Officers.
required_evidence: (xvi) the names, designations and other particulars of the Public Information Officers;

question: How often must the publications under Section 4(1)(b) be updated?
answer: Every year.
required_evidence: and thereafter update these publications every year;

question: What must a public authority publish while formulating important policies or announcing decisions affecting the public?
answer: All relevant facts.
required_evidence: publish all relevant facts while formulating important policies or announcing the decisions which affect public;

question: What must a public authority provide to affected persons regarding its administrative or quasi-judicial decisions?
answer: Reasons for its administrative or quasi-judicial decisions.
required_evidence: provide reasons for its administrative or quasi- judicial decisions to affected persons.

question: What does the Act say about suo motu disclosure by public authorities?
answer: It shall be a constant endeavour of every public authority to take steps to provide as much information suo motu to the public at regular intervals through various means of communications, including internet, so that the public have minimum resort to the use of this Act to obtain information.
required_evidence: It shall be a constant endeavour of every public authority to take steps in accordance with the requirements of clause (b) of sub-section (1) to provide as much information suo motu to the public at regular intervals through various means of communications, including internet, so that the public have minimum resort to the use of this Act to obtain information.

question: What does "disseminated" mean for the purposes of sub-sections (3) and (4) of Section 4?
answer: Making known or communicated the information to the public through notice boards, newspapers, public announcements, media broadcasts, the internet or any other means, including inspection of offices of any public authority.
required_evidence: "disseminated" means making known or communicated the information to the public through notice boards, newspapers, public announcements, media broadcasts, the internet or any other means, including inspection of offices of any public authority.

question: Within how many days of the enactment must every public authority designate Central Public Information Officers?
answer: One hundred days.
required_evidence: Every public authority shall, within one hundred days of the enactment of this Act, designate as many officers as the Central Public Information Officers or State Public Information Officers

question: Where must Assistant Public Information Officers be designated?
answer: At each sub-divisional level or other sub-district level.
required_evidence: every public authority shall designate an officer, within one hundred days of the enactment of this Act, at each sub-divisional level or other sub-district level as a Central Assistant Public Information Officer or a State Assistant Public Information Officer

question: What is the additional time period when an application is given to an Assistant Public Information Officer?
answer: Five days shall be added in computing the period for response.
required_evidence: a period of five days shall be added in computing the period for response specified under sub- section (1) of section 7.

question: What duty does a Public Information Officer have regarding persons seeking information?
answer: To deal with requests from persons seeking information and render reasonable assistance to the persons seeking such information.
required_evidence: Every Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, shall deal with requests from persons seeking information and render reasonable assistance to the persons seeking such information.

question: Can a Public Information Officer seek assistance from other officers?
answer: Yes, the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer may seek the assistance of any other officer as he or she considers necessary for the proper discharge of his or her duties.
required_evidence: The Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, may seek the assistance of any other officer as he or she considers it necessary for the proper discharge of his or her duties.

question: How is an officer whose assistance has been sought treated for the purposes of contravention of the Act?
answer: Such other officer shall be treated as a Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be.
required_evidence: for the purposes of any contravention of the provisions of this Act, such other officer shall be treated as a Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be.

question: In what languages can a request for information be made?
answer: In English or Hindi or in the official language of the area in which the application is being made.
required_evidence: shall make a request in writing or through electronic means in English or Hindi or in the official language of the area in which the application is being made

question: Is an applicant required to give reasons for requesting information?
answer: No.
required_evidence: An applicant making request for information shall not be required to give any reason for requesting the information or any other personal details except those that may be necessary for contacting him.

question: What must a public authority do if the information requested is held by another public authority?
answer: Transfer the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to that other public authority and inform the applicant immediately about such transfer.
required_evidence: the public authority, to which such application is made, shall transfer the application or such part of it as may be appropriate to that other public authority and inform the applicant immediately about such transfer

question: Within how many days must an application be transferred to another public authority?
answer: No later than five days from the date of receipt of the application.
required_evidence: the transfer of an application pursuant to this sub- section shall be made as soon as practicable but in no case later than five days from the date of receipt of the application.

question: Within how many days must a Public Information Officer provide information in normal course?
answer: Within thirty days of the receipt of the request.
required_evidence: in any case within thirty days of the receipt of the request, either provide the information on payment of such fee as may be prescribed or reject the request

question: Within how many hours must information concerning the life or liberty of a person be provided?
answer: Forty-eight hours.
required_evidence: where the information sought for concerns the life or liberty of a person, the same shall be provided within forty- eight hours of the receipt of the request.

question: What happens if the Public Information Officer fails to give a decision within the specified period?
answer: The Public Information Officer shall be deemed to have refused the request.
required_evidence: If the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, fails to give decision on the request for information within the period specified under sub-section (1), the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, shall be deemed to have refused the request.

question: What details must be included in an intimation when further fees are required?
answer: The details of further fees representing the cost of providing the information as determined by him, together with the calculations made to arrive at the amount in accordance with fee prescribed under sub-section (1), requesting him to deposit that fees.
required_evidence: the details of further fees representing the cost of providing the information as determined by him

question: What right does a person have regarding review of the decision as to the amount of fees charged?
answer: Information concerning his or her right with respect to review the decision as to the amount of fees charged or the form of access provided, including the particulars of the appellate authority, time limit, process and any other forms.
required_evidence: information concerning his or her right with respect to review the decision as to the amount of fees charged or the form of access provided, including the particulars of the appellate authority, time limit, process and any other forms.

question: What assistance must be provided to a sensorily disabled person seeking access to records?
answer: The Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer shall provide assistance to enable access to the information, including providing such assistance as may be appropriate for the inspection.
required_evidence: the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, shall provide assistance to enable access to the information, including providing such assistance as may be appropriate for the inspection.

question: Who is exempt from paying fees under the Act?
answer: Persons who are of below poverty line as may be determined by the appropriate Government.
required_evidence: no such fee shall be charged from the persons who are of below poverty line as may be determined by the appropriate Government.

question: When is information provided free of charge?
answer: Where a public authority fails to comply with the time limits specified in sub-section (1).
required_evidence: the person making request for the information shall be provided the information free of charge where a public authority fails to comply with the time limits specified in sub-section (1).

question: What must be communicated to a person when a request is rejected?
answer: The reasons for such rejection; the period within which an appeal against such rejection may be preferred; and the particulars of the appellate authority.
required_evidence: the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, shall communicate to the person making the request,— (i) the reasons for such rejection; (ii) the period within which an appeal against such rejection may be preferred; and (iii) the particulars of the appellate authority.

question: In what form shall information ordinarily be provided?
answer: In the form in which it is sought unless it would disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority or would be detrimental to the safety or preservation of the record in question.
required_evidence: An information shall ordinarily be provided in the form in which it is sought unless it would disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority or would be detrimental to the safety or preservation of the record in question.

question: What categories of information are exempt from disclosure under Section 8(1)(a)?
answer: Information, disclosure of which would prejudicially affect the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security, strategic, scientific or economic interests of the State, relation with foreign State or lead to incitement of an offence.
required_evidence: (a) information, disclosure of which would prejudicially affect the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security, strategic, scientific or economic interests of the State, relation with foreign State or lead to incitement of an offence;

question: What information is exempt under Section 8(1)(b)?
answer: Information which has been expressly forbidden to be published by any court of law or tribunal or the disclosure of which may constitute contempt of court.
required_evidence: (b) information which has been expressly forbidden to be published by any court of law or tribunal or the disclosure of which may constitute contempt of court;

question: What information is exempt under Section 8(1)(c)?
answer: Information, the disclosure of which would cause a breach of privilege of Parliament or the State Legislature.
required_evidence: (c) information, the disclosure of which would cause a breach of privilege of Parliament or the State Legislature;

question: Under what condition can information including commercial confidence, trade secrets or intellectual property be disclosed?
answer: Unless the competent authority is satisfied that larger public interest warrants the disclosure of such information.
required_evidence: (d) information including commercial confidence, trade secrets or intellectual property, the disclosure of which would harm the competitive position of a third party, unless the competent authority is satisfied that larger public interest warrants the disclosure of such information;

question: What information is exempt under Section 8(1)(e)?
answer: Information available to a person in his fiduciary relationship, unless the competent authority is satisfied that the larger public interest warrants the disclosure of such information.
required_evidence: (e) information available to a person in his fiduciary relationship, unless the competent authority is satisfied that the larger public interest warrants the disclosure of such information;

question: What information is exempt under Section 8(1)(f)?
answer: Information received in confidence from foreign Government.
required_evidence: (f) information received in confidence from foreign Government;

question: What information is exempt under Section 8(1)(g)?
answer: Information, the disclosure of which would endanger the life or physical safety of any person or identify the source of information or assistance given in confidence for law enforcement or security purposes.
required_evidence: (g) information, the disclosure of which would endanger the life or physical safety of any person or identify the source of information or assistance given in confidence for law enforcement or security purposes;

question: What information is exempt under Section 8(1)(h)?
answer: Information which would impede the process of investigation or apprehension or prosecution of offenders.
required_evidence: (h) information which would impede the process of investigation or apprehension or prosecution of offenders;

question: What is the exemption regarding cabinet papers under Section 8(1)(i)?
answer: Cabinet papers including records of deliberations of the Council of Ministers, Secretaries and other officers.
required_evidence: (i) cabinet papers including records of deliberations of the Council of Ministers, Secretaries and other officers:

question: When can decisions of the Council of Ministers and the reasons thereof be made public?
answer: After the decision has been taken, and the matter is complete, or over.
required_evidence: Provided that the decisions of Council of Ministers, the reasons thereof, and the material on the basis of which the decisions were taken shall be made public after the decision has been taken, and the matter is complete, or over

question: What personal information is exempt from disclosure under Section 8(1)(j)?
answer: Information which relates to personal information the disclosure of which has no relationship to any public activity or interest, or which would cause unwarranted invasion of the privacy of the individual unless the Central Public Information Officer or the State Public Information Officer or the appellate authority is satisfied that the larger public interest justifies the disclosure of such information.
required_evidence: (j) information which relates to personal information the disclosure of which has no relationship to any public activity or interest, or which would cause unwarranted invasion of the privacy of the individual unless the Central Public Information Officer or the State Public Information Officer or the appellate authority, as the case may be, is satisfied that the larger public interest justifies the disclosure of such information:

question: Can information be denied to Parliament or a State Legislature?
answer: No, the information which cannot be denied to the Parliament or a State Legislature shall not be denied to any person.
required_evidence: Provided that the information which cannot be denied to the Parliament or a State Legislature shall not be denied to any person.

question: Notwithstanding the Official Secrets Act, 1923, when may a public authority allow access to information?
answer: If public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests.
required_evidence: a public authority may allow access to information, if public interest in disclosure outweighs the harm to the protected interests.

question: After how many years is information relating to any occurrence, event or matter provided?
answer: Twenty years before the date on which any request is made.
required_evidence: any information relating to any occurrence, event or matter which has taken place, occurred or happened twenty years before the date on which any request is made under section 6 shall be provided to any person making a request under that section

question: What is the exception to the twenty-year rule under Section 8(3)?
answer: Subject to the provisions of clauses (a), (c) and (i) of sub-section (1).
required_evidence: Subject to the provisions of clauses (a), (c) and (i) of sub-section (1)

question: When may a Public Information Officer reject a request for information under Section 9?
answer: Where such a request for providing access would involve an infringement of copyright subsisting in a person other than the State.
required_evidence: a Central Public Information Officer or a State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, may reject a request for information where such a request for providing access would involve an infringement of copyright subsisting in a person other than the State.

question: What is severability under Section 10?
answer: Where a request for access to information is rejected on the ground that it is in relation to information which is exempt from disclosure, access may be provided to that part of the record which does not contain any information which is exempt from disclosure under this Act and which can reasonably be severed from any part that contains exempt information.
required_evidence: access may be provided to that part of the record which does not contain any information which is exempt from disclosure under this Act and which can reasonably be severed from any part that contains exempt information.

question: What must a notice to the applicant include when access is granted to a part of the record?
answer: That only part of the record requested, after severance of the record containing information which is exempt from disclosure, is being provided; the reasons for the decision; the name and designation of the person giving the decision; the details of the fees calculated; and his or her rights with respect to review of the decision.
required_evidence: the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, shall give a notice to the applicant, informing— (a) that only part of the record requested, after severance of the record containing information which is exempt from disclosure, is being provided;

question: Within how many days must a written notice be given to a third party when the Public Information Officer intends to disclose third party information?
answer: Within five days from the receipt of the request.
required_evidence: the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, shall, within five days from the receipt of the request, give a written notice to such third party

question: How many days does a third party have to make representation against proposed disclosure?
answer: Ten days from the date of receipt of such notice.
required_evidence: the third party shall, within ten days from the date of receipt of such notice, be given the opportunity to make representation against the proposed disclosure.

question: Within how many days must the Public Information Officer make a decision on third party information?
answer: Within forty days after receipt of the request under section 6.
required_evidence: the Central Public Information Officer or State Public Information Officer, as the case may be, shall, within forty days after receipt of the request under section 6, if the third party has been given an opportunity to make representation under sub-section (2), make a decision as to whether or not to disclose the information or record or part thereof

question: What must a notice to a third party under Section 11(3) include?
answer: A statement that the third party to whom the notice is given is entitled to prefer an appeal under section 19 against the decision.
required_evidence: A notice given under sub-section (3) shall include a statement that the third party to whom the notice is given is entitled to prefer an appeal under section 19 against the decision.

question: By what means does the Central Government constitute the Central Information Commission?
answer: By notification in the Official Gazette.
required_evidence: constitute a body to be known as the Central Information Commission

question: What is the composition of the Central Information Commission?
answer: The Chief Information Commissioner and such number of Central Information Commissioners, not exceeding ten, as may be deemed necessary.
required_evidence: The Central Information Commission shall consist of

question: Who appoints the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners?
answer: The President.
required_evidence: The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners shall be appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee

question: What is the composition of the committee that recommends appointments to the Central Information Commission?
answer: The Prime Minister, who shall be the Chairperson of the committee; the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha; and a Union Cabinet Minister to be nominated by the Prime Minister.
required_evidence: a committee consisting of— (i) the Prime Minister, who shall be the Chairperson of the committee; (ii) the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha; and (iii) a Union Cabinet Minister to be nominated by the Prime Minister.

question: Who is deemed to be the Leader of Opposition if no Leader of Opposition is recognised in the House of the People?
answer: The Leader of the single largest group in opposition of the Government in the House of the People.
required_evidence: where the Leader of Opposition in the House of the People has not been recognised as such, the Leader of the single largest group in opposition of the Government in the House of the People shall be deemed to be the Leader of Opposition.

question: What qualifications must the Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners possess?
answer: Persons of eminence in public life with wide knowledge and experience in law, science and technology, social service, management, journalism, mass media or administration and governance.
required_evidence: The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners shall be persons of eminence in public life with wide knowledge and experience in law, science and technology, social service, management, journalism, mass media or administration and governance.

question: What restrictions are placed on the Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner?
answer: Shall not be a Member of Parliament or Member of the Legislature of any State or Union territory, or hold any other office of profit or connected with any political party or carrying on any business or pursuing any profession.
required_evidence: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner shall not be a Member of Parliament or Member of the Legislature of any State or Union territory, as the case may be, or hold any other office of profit or connected with any political party or carrying on any business or pursuing any profession.

question: Where is the headquarters of the Central Information Commission?
answer: Delhi.
required_evidence: The headquarters of the Central Information Commission shall be at Delhi

question: For what term does the Chief Information Commissioner hold office?
answer: Five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
required_evidence: The Chief Information Commissioner shall hold office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office and shall not be eligible for reappointment

question: What is the maximum age for the Chief Information Commissioner to hold office?
answer: Sixty-five years.
required_evidence: Provided that no Chief Information Commissioner shall hold office as such after he has attained the age of sixty- five years.

question: For what term does an Information Commissioner hold office?
answer: Five years from the date on which he enters upon his office or till he attains the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier.
required_evidence: Every Information Commissioner shall hold office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office or till he attains the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier

question: Can an Information Commissioner be reappointed as an Information Commissioner?
answer: No, he shall not be eligible for reappointment as such Information Commissioner.
required_evidence: shall not be eligible for reappointment as such Information Commissioner

question: What is the maximum aggregate term if an Information Commissioner is appointed as the Chief Information Commissioner?
answer: Not more than five years in aggregate as the Information Commissioner and the Chief Information Commissioner.
required_evidence: where the Information Commissioner is appointed as the Chief Information Commissioner, his term of office shall not be more than five years in aggregate as the Information Commissioner and the Chief Information Commissioner.

question: Before whom must the Chief Information Commissioner make an oath or affirmation?
answer: The President or some other person appointed by him in that behalf.
required_evidence: The Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner shall before he enters upon his office make and subscribe before the President or some other person appointed by him in that behalf, an oath or affirmation
